## Where it comes from

A quail chick — round-bodied, short-beaked, feet planted. It
writes *w* (the "u" sound), which makes it one of the busiest
birds in the script: plurals, endings, and names all peep with
it. Its cursive twin is the coil
[Z7]({{ '/hieroglyphs/addenda/signs/z7/' | relative_url }}) —
same sound, quicker pen.

## How to remember it

The **chick** says *w* — the small round "oo" of a small round
bird. Wherever a word needs that vowel-ish glide, the chick
trots in on its two drawn legs.

Piece by piece:

- **w** — the chick, opening the title
- **t** — the loaf closing it: *wt,j*, the wrapper-of-mummies

Two signs name the man who bandaged the dead — and a chick leads
the word. The sign is taught in
<a href="{{ '/hieroglyphs/101/04-your-first-signs/' | relative_url }}">101's chapter 04</a>.
